title: Mutual Distillation Extracting Spatial-temporal Knowledge for Lightweight Multi-channel Sleep Stage Classification

problem.claim: Multi-channel sleep models provide rich spatial-temporal information but their increased size and computational costs constrain deployment on hardware devices.

gap.claim: Existing knowledge distillation methods do not fully extract and transfer spatial-temporal knowledge from multi-channel sleep signals.

contributions.claim: A general spatial-temporal mutual distillation framework is proposed for multi-channel sleep stage classification.
Spatial and temporal modules extract knowledge from human-body spatial relationships and sleep-signal temporal transition rules for transfer from a large teacher model to a lightweight student model.
The mutual distillation framework enables teacher and student models to learn from each other.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On the ISRUC-III and MASS-SS3 datasets, the authors report effective model compression with minimal performance loss.
The authors report state-of-the-art performance compared with baseline methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Sleep stage classification is clinically significant, and multi-channel signals are used for their rich spatial-temporal information.
Multi-channel models increase model size and computational cost, limiting hardware application.
Existing distillation methods are described as insufficient for extracting and transferring spatial-temporal knowledge.
The proposed framework uses spatial and temporal modules with mutual teacher-student distillation.
Experiments on two datasets are reported to achieve effective compression, minimal performance loss, and state-of-the-art baseline comparisons.

source_observation.claim: The framework explicitly models spatial relationships and temporal transition rules during knowledge distillation.

interpretation.claim: Compression may preserve task-relevant structured knowledge better when distillation reflects domain-specific spatial and temporal dependencies.

application.claim: For other structured multichannel time-series tasks, distillation objectives could incorporate known spatial relationships and temporal dynamics.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach transfers to domains without comparable spatial structure or temporal transition rules.

unknowns: Reported compression ratios, performance metrics, and loss values are unspecified.
The baseline methods and hardware deployment conditions are unspecified.
The distillation objectives and module architectures are unspecified.
